# Lessons from Part V {.unnumbered}

TODO Part V capstone — Lessons from Graphs

Themes to draw out (match the depth of lessons_4):

- Representation shapes the algorithm — adjacency list vs. matrix is
  not a storage choice; it changes which questions are cheap. The
  choice cascades through every algorithm in the part.
- Relaxation as the unifying technique — Dijkstra, Bellman-Ford,
  Floyd-Warshall, and Prim's MST all maintain an upper-bound estimate
  and tighten it repeatedly. The difference between them is the
  order in which they consider edges.
- The cut property — MST correctness reduces to a single graph
  theorem; Kruskal and Prim are two orderings of the same proof.
- DFS is the swiss-army knife for structural questions —
  connectivity, cycles, topological order, strongly connected
  components, bridges, articulation points. All of them are DFS
  plus a small bookkeeping tweak.
- Flow as constructive duality — max-flow min-cut is LP-duality made
  fully visible. The augmenting-path procedure is the constructive
  half of the proof.

Part VI picks up the DP thread — the Floyd-Warshall grid from chapter 35

condensation from chapter 37 turns a directed graph into a DAG on which
